title: Inventory and order the general encounter-generation dependencies
proposedRouting: Build and maintain a dependency-readiness map from general reusable owners through runtime composition. Create or route missing owner tickets before any generated-patient or cohort ticket can become actionable.
guidance: Audit stable identities/ownership/provenance first; then reusable history, symptom, function, safety, substance, MSE, physical, vital/measurement, condition/chart, reaction, regimen, prior-trial, treatment-history, demographic, and context records; then labs/panels/reference intervals and result generators, imaging/electrical studies/instruments, reveal actions/services, medications, therapies, and dispositions; then diagnosis/intervention dossiers and cross-topic relationships; then reviewed policies, prerequisites, fit/interactions, balance, and traces; then recipe/instance/resolver/replay/persistence/validation mechanics. A thin MDD, GAD, or other dossier may be used early to discover dependencies, but missing general owners must not be replaced by case-specific prose. The gate does not demand all of psychiatry. It requires the smallest coherent general slice for the intended encounter, with every deferred gap explicit and nonexecutable. Runtime patient generation and seed-cohort calibration stay last.
reviewerNotes: Reviewer approved MDD as the first deep database dependency vertical with no setting, difficulty, or treatment-intensity ceiling, and approved general dependencies before specific case work. The 2026-07-28 readiness audit found useful identity, service, test, medication, treatment, compatibility-state, replay, and persistence foundations, but no canonical finding catalog: five approved/review case files contain 621 nested finding occurrences, 186 IDs, and 112 IDs reused across files. The ordered missing-owner queue is recorded in docs/ENCOUNTER_GENERATION_DEPENDENCIES.md. Do not generate patients or hide a missing general owner in case prose.
resurfacingTrigger: Before prioritizing a patient/case generator, generated cohort, or case-specific workaround over a missing reusable dependency owner.

title: Create the canonical reusable finding-definition boundary
proposedRouting: Add the smallest versioned catalog and Zod boundary for one canonical atomic finding, its admissible typed value, one resolved patient value, and contributor provenance. Keep reveal actions, tests, tendencies, and points in separate owners.
guidance: This ticket implements the identity/ownership half of D-170 only. A finding definition owns stable identity, neutral labels, aliases, semantic kind, value shape, and allowed presentation projections. A resolved finding owns one frozen value plus explicit contributing owner IDs and resolution metadata. It does not own prevalence, diagnosis criteria, medication fit, test cost, clinical relevance, or points. Preserve existing FindingBlueprint and CaseInstance snapshots as the compatibility path; do not migrate cases, generate a patient, or add clinical content in this slice.
reviewerNotes: Approved architecture: anything reused across files should have one canonical owner, while player-facing screens may blend projections and the backend must keep the atomic fact and contributors separable. Implemented as an additive compatibility boundary with one identity-only, medically unreviewed depressed-mood seed. Existing case-local findings and saved snapshots remain unchanged.
resurfacingTrigger: Before normalizing repeated finding IDs, implementing the shared-finding compiler, or adding a reusable clinical fact to another case.

resolution.note: Added strict versioned schemas for canonical finding identity, admissible outcome values, unresolved versus known values, contributor provenance, and resolution trace; registered one identity-only depressed-mood definition; added exact registry/catalog validation and compatibility tests. No case migration, generation behavior, diagnosis association, probability, relevance, scoring, treatment implication, or medical approval was added.

title: Normalize the first wide, shallow psychiatry finding seed
proposedRouting: Inventory the 186 current case-local finding IDs, normalize exact duplicates and aliases, then add only the wide, shallow reusable identity bins needed for general psychiatric history, symptoms, function, safety, substance use, MSE, and physical examination.
guidance: This is an identity and granularity review, not a diagnostic manual. Each accepted seed entry receives a stable definition file with concise swappable presentation metadata. It gains no prevalence, condition association, cardinality, randomization probability, scoring relevance, or treatment implication in this ticket. Preserve unknown separately from absent. Do not merge superficially similar concepts when their time scope, source, or value semantics differ; route ambiguous merges for psychiatrist review. A missing concept receives a candidate bin rather than being embedded in an MDD-specific file.
reviewerNotes: Approved by Dustin Rowland. P1-P6: use one canonical identity per independently resolvable truth; treat interchangeable wording as aliases rather than identities; keep facts distinct when time, source, value, or coexistence can differ; route structured records, measurements, and test results to their real owners; add only unambiguous identities from the 37-candidate tranche; and add no clinical association, criterion, probability, point, migration, or approval. The implementation registers 27 medically unreviewed identity-only definitions, including the existing depressed-mood seed. Ten candidates remain explicitly unresolved because their value type or semantic boundary is not yet safe to encode. Existing case and save snapshots remain untouched.
resurfacingTrigger: After the canonical finding schema exists and before migrating repeated case-local findings or authoring diagnosis-specific finding tendencies.

resolution.note: Registered 27 identity-only canonical findings: one existing seed plus 26 new definitions across function, depressive and anxiety history, current mania-history projections, reported psychosis, sleep/appetite, and suicide/violence safety. Every entry remains medically unreviewed and point-free. Duration and subjective burden were not forced into outcome values; ambiguous interest/pleasure, fatigue/energy, grandiosity, impulsivity/high-risk behavior, preparatory-behavior timing, weapon fact versus concern, paranoia/persecution, and reported versus observed disorganization remain review items. No compatibility case, resolved patient, generator, scoring rule, or UI was changed.

title: Normalize diminished interest and pleasure as anhedonia
proposedRouting: Create one source-scoped canonical identity for current self-reported anhedonia. Treat loss or reduction of interest and loss or reduction of pleasure as interchangeable presentation aliases for this game's focused decision horizon.
guidance: Current compatibility content treats loss of interest, reduced interest, reduced enjoyment, and anhedonia as interchangeable descriptions. Final policy P1: preserve one backend identity, `finding.history.current-anhedonia`. Final policy P2: loss or reduction of interest and loss or reduction of pleasure are aliases for that identity because this distinction does not usually affect PsychSim's focused best-next-step decision. Final policy P3: source units retain their original permitted wording and provenance, so a later decision-specific need can reopen and split the identity without losing the source trail. Final policy P4: this decision adds an identity shell only—no MDD criterion, cardinality, diagnosis inference, generation tendency, probability, relevance, points, treatment implication, migration, or medical approval.
reviewerNotes: Dustin Rowland directed: blend loss of interest and loss of pleasure as two descriptions for anhedonia because that level of granularity usually does not matter for decision-making. Existing compatibility cases remain unchanged.
resurfacingTrigger: Before migrating `finding.depressive.anhedonia`, attaching diagnosis criteria, or compiling diminished-interest and diminished-pleasure contributors into a resolved patient.

resolution.note: Added one medically unreviewed, identity-only `finding.history.current-anhedonia` definition with conservative loss/reduction-of-interest and loss/reduction-of-pleasure aliases. No case migration, clinical association, criterion, generation behavior, probability, point value, treatment implication, or UI change was added.

title: Separate subjective energy complaints from their contributors
proposedRouting: Create one broad current self-reported fatigue/low-energy identity without replacing the distinct facts that can produce that report. Route standardized responses and unstructured patient wording through a separate, contributor-preserving presentation projection.
guidance: Final P1: `finding.history.current-fatigue-low-energy` represents only the broad subjective report that fatigue, low energy, or tiredness is present. Final P2: daytime sleepiness or somnolence, muscular weakness, psychomotor slowing, medication sedation, exertional intolerance, and later reviewed contributors remain separately resolved patient facts; the umbrella report neither identifies nor erases its cause. Final P3: a standardized instrument or item owns an explicit reviewed mapping from applicable resolved facts to its yes/no/ordinal response. Final P4: unstandardized history uses a deterministic response bank whose phrases may intentionally overlap across different source facts. Final P5: every projected response is resolved before play and saves the exact source-finding IDs, mapping version, and chosen wording variant so the post-submit audit can disentangle patient truth, assessment response, and surface wording. Final P6: aliases never create these mappings, purchasing only reveals the frozen response, and this decision adds no diagnosis criterion, generation probability, relevance, points, treatment behavior, compatibility migration, or medical approval.
reviewerNotes: Dustin Rowland approved the broad fatigue/low-energy/tiredness grouping with an important scalability clarification: a patient may have any of several distinct underlying facts and describe any of them with the same ordinary energy language. Standardized assessments should record their defined response, while unstandardized history should draw from a shared wording bank. The backend and explanation system must retain the distinct source facts.
resurfacingTrigger: Before compiling a subjective energy response, adding a standardized energy item, or allowing any surface phrase or canonical alias to imply sleepiness, weakness, slowing, sedation, exertional intolerance, diagnosis, or points.

resolution.note: Added one medically unreviewed identity shell for the broad current self-reported fatigue/low-energy complaint. Distinct possible contributors were not merged or added as aliases. Recorded the required three-layer architecture—resolved source facts, assessment response, and surface wording—and routed its typed many-to-many projection contract to a separate blocking technical ticket. No projection compiler, case migration, clinical association, probability, point value, treatment behavior, or medical approval was added.

title: Model subjective assessment responses and overlapping patient wording
proposedRouting: Add a point-free, versioned projection boundary between resolved patient facts and player-facing assessment responses or wording. Keep identity aliases strict while allowing reviewed phrase banks to overlap across source facts.
guidance: A FindingExpressionBank owns stable wording-variant IDs and lawful display channels, not clinical truth. A FindingRevealProjection explicitly names its source finding IDs, applicable action or instrument item, source outcomes, response mapping, and expression bank. A frozen resolved projection saves the projection version, response value, selected wording-variant ID, source action or instrument, and every contributing resolved-finding ID before play. Standardized instruments retain their own response scale, interpretation, and rights boundary. Unstructured wording may be deliberately ambiguous. Neither aliases nor phrase similarity may create a mapping, and neither displayed wording nor the number of contributors may affect scoring. The later explanation trace must reconstruct source fact → reviewed projection → displayed response without using the presentation as a diagnostic inference.
reviewerNotes: Accepted architecture from Dustin Rowland's fatigue clarification. The technical implementation must scale to many-to-many language while preserving the concise, question-bank-like player presentation and a fully separable backend audit.
resurfacingTrigger: Before the shared-finding compiler projects one resolved fact into an action, a standardized item derives a response, or unstructured history reuses the same patient phrase for several possible facts.

title: Separate current from historical grandiosity
proposedRouting: Create separate current and past/lifetime episodic grandiosity identities because their values can disagree. Let history actions present them together while preserving both values and their time scopes.
guidance: Proposed P1: current grandiosity and a history of grandiosity during a prior possible mood episode are separate facts because either may be present without the other. Proposed P2: a Mania/Hypomania History action may reveal both in one compact section, but the backend and explanation trace retain their separate IDs, values, time scopes, and contributors. Proposed P3: phrases such as grandiosity or inflated self-esteem belong to the new presentation vocabulary and may be used within either time scope; wording alone never chooses the identity. Proposed P4: this establishes identity shells only—no mania criterion, episode inference, generation tendency, probability, points, treatment implication, compatibility migration, or medical approval. Review question Q3: approve separate current and past/lifetime episodic grandiosity identities?
reviewerNotes: Prepared as the next one-at-a-time semantic boundary after the fatigue decision established that overlapping patient wording must not collapse distinct patient truths.
resurfacingTrigger: Before migrating `finding.mania.grandiosity`, attaching a mania-history criterion, or projecting grandiosity wording without an explicit current versus historical time scope.

title: Add typed vital, measurement, MSE, and physical-exam owners
proposedRouting: Create reusable typed observation and measurement definitions for basic vitals, anthropometrics, MSE, and physical findings, with a compatibility projection for current string-valued opening vitals.
guidance: The technical boundary must distinguish categorical observations from numeric measurements and preserve unit, precision, reference or interpretation metadata, temporal/source scope, and one resolved value. Weight/BMI and body habitus remain distinct. A neutral finding such as recorded weight does not receive an abnormal color merely because it is present. This ticket does not choose medical reference ranges, incidental probabilities, diagnosis associations, or scoring. Those require source- and rule-specific review.
reviewerNotes: Approved direction: every reusable physical, MSE, vital, and anthropometric fact should be structured and auditable; player presentation may remain concise and should not imply that mere presence is abnormal.
resurfacingTrigger: Before runtime-generated vitals, reusable MSE/physical results, or migration away from PatientOpening.basicVitals string arrays.

title: Complete the structured result boundary for every test kind
proposedRouting: Extend the per-test-file model with JSON-safe structured result contracts for numeric panels and currently patient-owned studies, while preserving patient-authored critical overrides and immediate reveal/service behavior.
guidance: The current numeric laboratory generator remains a compatibility foundation. ECG, imaging, EEG, toxicology, medication levels, pregnancy testing, and pharmacogenomics need typed component or interpretation shapes so a patient owns resolved values rather than a memorable prose paragraph. Test definitions own result shape and lawful generation profiles; the patient or encounter recipe owns critical abnormalities and overrides; reveal actions own menu presentation and cost; scoring owns relevance. This ticket adds no result ranges, sensitivity, specificity, abnormal probability, case-defining value, or points.
reviewerNotes: Approved architecture: each test has its own reusable file and generates or renders a patient-specific structured value, with reference and abnormality details auditable after play.
resurfacingTrigger: Before a patient-owned study is randomized, reused across generated patients, or consumed by the shared-finding compiler.

title: Separate and version the reusable resolved patient-state records
proposedRouting: Compose the existing reaction, regimen, trial, treatment-history, context, and diagnosis compatibility shapes into a point-free versioned patient-state boundary that separates internal condition truth from chart diagnosis claims.
guidance: This schema slice owns resolved state only. Internal ConditionState records, uncertain or duplicated chart DiagnosisRecordEntry values, independently targetable regimen entries, structured prior trials, reaction assessment, treatment history, demographics/context, canonical findings, and measurements must remain distinct and composable. A chart label never activates an internal condition by itself. The boundary must scale to multiple diagnoses, long trial histories, duplicate medications, supplements, and nonpsychiatric medications. Do not add PatientTemplate generation, clinical inference, optional-comorbidity selection, scoring, or migration of historical attempts in this ticket.
reviewerNotes: Approved direction: complex patients may have numerous uncertain chart diagnoses, many current medications and prior trials, while the focused encounter still asks only for the best next step. Preserve all state without grading an exhaustive plan.
resurfacingTrigger: Before implementing PatientInstance, optional comorbidity selection, generated regimens/trials, or chart-versus-internal diagnosis behavior.

title: Define reusable substance and background-exposure state
proposedRouting: Create stable substance/background-exposure identities and a typed resolved-use state that can represent none, unknown, use pattern, recency, intoxication, withdrawal, and patient attribution without automatically assigning a diagnosis.
guidance: The foundation must support prescription, nonprescription, supplement, nicotine, alcohol, caffeine, and other substance exposure without forcing all identities into the medication treatment menu. A positive use fact, intoxication state, withdrawal state, substance-induced diagnosis, and clinician attribution are separate concepts. This ticket does not set age distributions, prevalence, symptom associations, diagnostic thresholds, treatment routes, or points. Those become bounded source and psychiatrist-review tickets after the state vocabulary is accepted.
reviewerNotes: Standing direction: substance use is commonly relevant and must support muddy attribution, but random texture alone must not silently diagnose a substance-induced disorder. The generator later reveals pre-resolved state; purchasing history never creates it.
resurfacingTrigger: After the resolved patient-state boundary exists and before substance exposure can be generated, influence a diagnosis, or change treatment scoring.

title: Compile focused encounter rubrics from reusable decision policies
proposedRouting: Define the reusable, versioned decision-policy catalog and pure compiler boundary that selects one focused broad route, treatment-triggered prerequisites, fit, interaction, safety, parsimony, and disposition contributors into a CompiledRubric.
guidance: This ticket is compiler architecture, not clinical authoring. A policy references reviewed stable owners and constrained predicates; only decision-relevant positive rules plus global safety/interaction rules enter one focused snapshot. It preserves provenance, specificity, issue/effect IDs, rule-combination outcomes, engine-inferred labels, and coverage diagnostics. Missing clinical direction creates a ticket and no default penalty. Existing case-local scoring and reference runs remain unchanged until separately migrated. Do not create MDD treatment guidance, point values, a general-purpose expression language, or generated encounters in this slice.
reviewerNotes: Approved model: the broad primary decision owns most points, smaller goodness-of-fit contributors may stack, history/workup misses are bounded, and one critical error cannot be outweighed by many minor bonuses. Clinical rule approval and provisional balance remain separate.
resurfacingTrigger: After reusable patient/test/intervention owners exist and before PatientTemplate can compile an encounter rubric or a diagnosis dossier activates shared scoring.

title: Compile patient instances from reusable catalog owners
proposedRouting: Prepare the versioned PatientTemplate → PatientInstance → EncounterInstance and CompiledRubric boundary while preserving CaseBlueprint as a historical compatibility snapshot. Do not activate generation until the reusable finding, condition, intervention, test, regimen/trial, context, and policy dependencies can be resolved deterministically.
guidance: The diagnosis family owns reusable disorder knowledge, including MDD mild, moderate, and severe branches across outpatient, hospital, polypharmacy, ECT, ketamine, and other later contexts. It owns no encounter difficulty, play time, setting ceiling, or complexity budget. PatientTemplate is the current technical name for a source-controlled case/encounter recipe: it selects setting, a focused next-step question, condition states, optional pools, regimen/history constraints, available actions, an encounter complexity envelope, and narrow overrides without copying generic diagnosis, intervention, or test knowledge. Authoring prepares all required static files rather than checking in resolved patients. After the dependency gate is complete, the pure browser engine will build and persist a complete PatientInstance and EncounterInstance from approved inputs plus a seed at queue-fill or explicit refresh time. Historical attempts retain their original CaseBlueprint snapshots.
reviewerNotes: Approved architecture direction: variants of one underlying disorder remain in one diagnosis-family record. Reviewer correction: the reusable MDD dossier must not own P7-style encounter duration or difficulty and must scale to hospital, polypharmacy, ECT, ketamine, and other contexts. Do not generate patients yet. First prepare the dependency files; the deterministic in-game engine later constructs resolved encounters from those files and the encounter recipe's complexity budget.
resurfacingTrigger: Before adding another case-authored diagnosis severity model, assigning setting/difficulty/complexity to a diagnosis dossier, pre-generating a patient inventory, or activating the target runtime compiler before its reusable dependencies are ready.

title: Resolve shared findings once with contributor provenance
proposedRouting: Implement a deterministic compiler pass that resolves each source fact once, retains every contributor and conflict outcome, and then creates separately saved assessment/wording projections for each relevant player-facing result.
guidance: A concentration problem may contribute to both anxiety and depressive-symptom displays; several distinct facts may also contribute to one subjective energy response and share deliberately ambiguous wording. The backend must save every atomic source fact, the exact reviewed source-to-response projection, all contributing resolved-finding IDs, and the stable selected wording variant. Explicit critical constraints, syndrome/cardinality requirements, weighted tendencies, and background variation remain distinguishable. File order never chooses a winner. Hard contradictions retry deterministically or quarantine; they are not patched with prose. Alias or phrase similarity cannot create a projection. Purchasing information reveals an already frozen response, and wording cannot alter diagnosis, scoring, or treatment logic. The explanation system must reconstruct source fact → projection rule → displayed response while showing which diagnosis, medication, context, optional module, or patient override contributed to the underlying values.
reviewerNotes: Approved architecture direction: influences may blend in the player presentation, but every fact and contributor must remain separable in the backend and post-submit explanation. Dustin Rowland further clarified that distinct underlying findings may produce the same standardized energy response or ordinary patient wording; this many-to-many projection must be explicit, deterministic, frozen before play, and auditable.
resurfacingTrigger: Before one symptom or observation can appear in multiple screens, before optional comorbidities are enabled, or before diagnosis-owned constraints are compiled into patients.

title: Define a bounded presentation-richness envelope
proposedRouting: Define a template-specific presentation envelope plus a psychiatry-referral plausibility check, then calibrate clean and deliberately muddy reference cohorts. Keep the immediate question legible while allowing bounded condition-selection groups, extensive structured prior treatment, uncertain chart labels, overlapping symptom counts, and whole-patient fit rules.
guidance: Focused means a bounded best-next-step decision, not a simple or diagnostically clean patient. Required conditions, current regimen, and decision-relevant prior history sit outside the optional-texture budget. A template may select a bounded number of condition modules from an explicit patient-family pool. Resolved findings may superficially satisfy several symptom checklists and must not be deleted or redrawn for that reason; only a required or selected module creates internal condition truth. Chart diagnoses and rule-outs remain separate. Prolonged or severe psychiatry-referral presentations require multiple structured prior efforts by default, with no small global cap; a treatment-naive exception requires a template reason. Reject generation only for malformed or literally contradictory same-scope state. Missing treatment, disposition, investigation, or rubric coverage is a nonblocking diagnostic and ticket, not a reason to remove the patient. Clinical tendencies, game weights, and point mappings remain separately reviewed.
reviewerNotes: Reviewer correction: this is a psychiatry simulator, so prolonged or severe presentations should virtually always include multiple prior treatments or coping attempts rather than zero or one. Cases may request a bounded comorbidity draw such as one to three diagnoses from an explicit list. Do not sweep for superficial diagnostic thresholds and remove overlapping symptoms: many psychiatric patients plausibly satisfy parts or even raw symptom counts of several disorders, while attribution, time course, substances, and not-better-explained clauses determine the modeled condition. The system must support uncertain and numerous diagnoses, long medication histories, polypharmacy, and treatment choices that cover several plausible formulations. Keep the immediate decision focused and auditable rather than making the patient artificially simple. Final clarification: do not use an undefined no-safe-route concept to reject generated patients. Start permissively and flag individual encounters after play; only literal impossibility or incompatibility, such as one same-scope fact holding mutually exclusive values, should invalidate generation.
resurfacingTrigger: Before enabling deterministic optional-feature selection or using richness requirements to accept, retry, or quarantine a generated patient.

title: Present all studies under one searchable Testing tab
proposedRouting: Change the player-facing navigation to History → Physical exam → Testing → Diagnosis → Treatment. Testing presents labs, imaging, ECG, EEG, and named instruments in one searchable list while backend study kind, service, fulfillment, result schema, cost, and provenance remain intact.
guidance: This is a presentation grouping, not a schema flattening. A test definition still owns whether it is a laboratory assay, image, electrical study, or structured instrument; service fulfillment still determines in-house versus sendout cost. Search must include neutral aliases and metadata without exposing case relevance. Existing saved action IDs and historical receipts must remain replayable.
reviewerNotes: Approved player workflow: History, Physical exam, Testing, Diagnosis, Treatment. Put labs, imaging, ECGs, and specific scales in the single Testing tab to keep the interface legible.
resurfacingTrigger: Before changing investigation-category schemas or adding another player-facing tab for a new study type.

title: Verify DRS-R-98 identity, version, and reuse boundary
proposedRouting: Register the instrument and primary validation sources, establish reproduction and scoring rights, and separately review when it is a fair high-effort Testing option. Do not copy items or call one score definitive before those gates are resolved.
guidance: The requested game role is a universally searchable named assessment that can provide strong information in an appropriate delirium-versus-dementia snapshot at substantial effort/point cost. Identity, version, population, administration requirements, score interpretation, validation performance, and exact item-reuse permission must remain separate. The player-facing result may later be only a score if that is clinically and legally supportable, while internal structured derivation remains auditable. The instrument must not be relevant to routine uncomplicated outpatient patients merely because it is searchable.
resurfacingTrigger: Before adding DRS-R-98 to the universal Testing catalog, reproducing any instrument wording, or awarding points for its use.

title: Source eating-disorder medical-instability disposition rules
proposedRouting: Select a current authoritative eating-disorder source and extract a focused set of medical-instability and level-of-care contributors. Preserve BMI as one typed measurement rather than letting a single cutoff silently determine hospitalization.
guidance: The proposed snapshot can randomize a case-authored BMI and ask whether close outpatient care or hospital-level evaluation is the best next step, but level of care may also depend on vital signs, laboratory or ECG abnormalities, intake trajectory, acute symptoms, suicidality, and available supports. The source review must identify which contributors are appropriate for the game's setting and focused horizon, which are hard gates versus weighted concerns, and which tests must be accessible. No threshold, diagnosis rule, disposition, or point value is authorized by this ticket.
resurfacingTrigger: Before creating an anorexia patient family, generating a case-defining BMI, or grading outpatient versus hospital disposition.

title: Design a focused anorexia level-of-care patient family
proposedRouting: After the medical-instability rule is reviewed, compile one question-bank snapshot whose primary decision is proportionate level of care. Add only bounded comorbid conditions and medication-fit contributors that do not obscure that decision.
guidance: The patient family may vary BMI and other reviewed stability facts, then compile an outpatient or hospital-evaluation route from the resolved state. Comorbid depression or bipolar disorder may later contribute separately traceable medication-fit effects, including appetite or weight concerns, but those bonuses cannot override an unsafe disposition and must use their own reviewed diagnosis and medication rules. The case should not demand a complete eating-disorder treatment plan or simulate longitudinal restoration.
resurfacingTrigger: After an eating-disorder medical-instability policy is reviewable and before adding a generated anorexia patient to any runtime pool.

title: Select and intake the current CANMAT bipolar guidance
proposedRouting: Identify the current canonical CANMAT/ISBD bipolar I and bipolar II guideline documents plus corrections or updates, register rights and scope, and create bounded recommendation-level review packets before changing either reviewer patient.
guidance: Bipolar depression, mania, bipolar I, and bipolar II require related but nonidentical source mappings. The intake must preserve publication version, population, phase, jurisdiction, recommendation identifiers, evidence strength where supplied, and any update or corrigendum relationships. A guideline record does not itself activate a treatment route or point value. This foundational source should be reviewed before using bipolar comorbidity to create appetite/weight medication-fit bonuses in other patient families.
resurfacingTrigger: Before changing bipolar-depression or acute-mania treatment guidance, or using bipolar treatment rules as a modifier in another generated patient.
